tasks.short: Collect labour-market and industry figures for pay, flex and hiring.

today.trigger: A recruiter, the Compensation and Benefits Specialist or the HR Director asks what the market is doing, or the analyst's own weekly scan is due.
steps: Open CBS, UWV and the current CAO pages, plus the latest rate cards from the three staffing agencies.
Copy wage, vacancy and unemployment figures into an Excel workbook by site and role family.
Skim field comments from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo and file purchased salary surveys on SharePoint.
Send a short mail with the clippings attached.
drudgery: Retyping tables from PDFs and web pages
Chasing the latest agency rate card
Reformatting figures so the three sites can be compared
today.time_sinks: Most of the hour and a half each week goes to finding and retyping figures, then to making warehouse and transport roles comparable across the three sites.

lenses.faster: Searching, downloading and retyping public tables and rate cards disappears. What stays is about 50 minutes a week: checking every cited figure and holding any conversation with an agency.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly schedule, and a new file in the source folder, starts the run. The filing and the draft brief finish on their own. The analyst gates the brief before C&B, a recruiter or the HR Director uses it.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift supervisors get a labour-supply note for flex orders at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, a group that today hears the market only through the office. Demand would grow in peak season, when flex headcount moves between 150 and 300 and each site wants its own note.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying CBS tables and agency cards into Excel. The analyst gets more time to judge whether a move in the local market should change a vacancy's pay or the size of the flex order.
lenses.options: A CBS-only brief, a brief that adds UWV vacancy pressure, and a brief that adds the three agency rate cards can point to different actions: raise a CAO band, order more flex, or leave pay unchanged. The drafts change the decision, so all three are kept until the analyst picks one.
lenses.altitude: The week starts from a filed brief instead of a search. The analyst gains the right to mark a source as approved for HR use. The job becomes more expert on whether a figure is comparable, and less of it is clerical.
reach: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist's first collection of market wage figures. The analyst would need the CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer scales and the warehouse CAO allowances well enough to file them against Noordhaven's bands.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which source the OR, the CAO parties and the Compensation and Benefits Specialist will treat as fair, and when a national survey does not describe shift work in Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo. That judgment, and any conversation with an agency, stays with the person. A model can draft from files already stored; it cannot decide that a source is fit for a pay conversation.
tasks.pattern_why: The source list is known, so an open-ended agent is unnecessary. Public tables and dropped files land in one folder, and one model call turns those files into a brief with a citation on every figure. The person checks the brief before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: Every Monday morning, and whenever an agency rate card or a purchased survey is saved into the agreed SharePoint folder.
steps: A scheduled job files the agreed CBS and UWV tables and watches the folder for agency cards and purchased surveys.
One model call writes a Dutch brief that cites a stored file for every figure and splits warehouse and transport roles by site.
The brief offers the three source sets side by side: public statistics, public statistics plus vacancies, and those plus agency rates.
The analyst checks each figure against the stored file and strips names, phone numbers and email addresses from vacancy text.
The approved brief is mailed to the agreed list and filed with the source set that was chosen.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the brief, including which source set is fit to use, before it goes to C&B, recruiters or the HR Director. Calls with the three agencies stay with a person.
data_needed: Agreed CBS and UWV tables for the Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo labour-market areas
Current CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer scales and the warehouse CAO allowances
Agency rate cards from the three staffing agencies
Role families used in Recruitee
Purchased survey extracts where the licence allows this use
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint source log next to the brief: file name, public URL or licence reference, retrieval date, model name, and the analyst who approved it.

evidence.claim: Uber's QueryGPT cut a query from about 10 minutes to about 3, and 78% of early users said it saved time, while hallucinated table and column names remained unsolved. A brief that copies figures needs the same kind of check.
Microsoft reports that faster access to workforce information does not, by itself, lead to better decisions.
Workday's published workforce trend report does not establish how much of the change AI caused. External trend prose needs the same caution.
The digest contains no Dutch result for an HR analyst automating collection of labour-market reports.

risks: A model can place a real source link beside a wage or vacancy figure it mis-copied, and a busy reader will trust the link.
Agency contracts and purchased surveys may forbid uploading the file to a model even when an employee may read it.
Vacancy text often contains names and phone numbers. Stored without a purpose, that is personal data under the AVG.
Trend wording can imply a cause of a hiring or pay change that the tables do not support.
research_questions: Do the three agency contracts and the current survey licences allow a model to read and summarise those files?
In the last four quarters, did an external figure change a pay band, a flex order or a vacancy, or did the agencies' advice decide it?
Can the analyst verify every cited number in the weekly brief inside the 50 minutes that remain?

tasks.short: Tell people when a report, tool or metric definition changes.

today.trigger: A Power BI report, an AFAS field or a certified measure changes, or a manager asks why a number moved.
steps: Write down what changed in the dataset, the measure or the extract.
Draft a Dutch Teams post or Outlook mail for HR business partners and the managers who use the report.
Update the SharePoint page that lists reports and definitions.
Answer the same follow-up questions one by one in Teams.
drudgery: Rewriting the same explanation for each site
Looking up who actually uses the report
Updating screenshots and old SharePoint pages
today.time_sinks: Drafting the note and then repeating it in chat takes longer than making the change to the report.

lenses.faster: The first draft and the hunt for the distribution list disappear. What stays is about 55 minutes of the weekly hour and a half: editing the Dutch note and deciding who should receive it.
lenses.autonomous: A change to a certified measure, report or AFAS field used by the dataset starts the run. The draft note is written on its own from the change record. The analyst gates the wording and the audience before anything is sent.
lenses.ambitious: A definition that changes a number managers use is explained the day it ships, instead of at the next monthly HR meeting. That decision, whether a change is material, happens far more often. Demand would grow if every tiny metadata edit also raised a note, and that growth would make the channel useless, so the trigger stays limited to changes in certified numbers.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping the same Teams explanation for three sites. The analyst gets more of the conversations where a definition change actually changes a manager's decision.
lenses.options: Three drafts change the outcome: a short note to HR business partners only, a full note to site leads, and a decision to hold the metric back until the OR has been informed. Picking the draft decides who acts on the new number and who keeps using the old one.
lenses.altitude: Change notes queue up after each publish instead of being written from scratch. The analyst gains the right to hold a changed metric back from managers until the note is approved. The job becomes more expert on the meaning of a change and less of a messenger.
reach: The HR Business Partner's routine of passing dashboard changes to site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. The analyst would need each site's audience list and the works council's information routine.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which wording a warehouse manager will misread, which changes are material to a decision, and which description of a dashboard is something the works council should hear before managers do. The person approves the Dutch text and the audience. The model only drafts from the change record.
tasks.pattern_why: Every enhancement follows the same path: a structured change record in, one Dutch note out, a person sends it. The prose is the only messy step, so one model call is enough. Deciding the audience and posting the mail needs no agent and no open-ended search.

in_practice.trigger: A certified measure, a report definition or an AFAS field that feeds the dataset is changed in the metric register.
steps: The register records the object, the old wording, the new wording, the effective refresh and the reports that use it.
One model call drafts a Dutch note that uses only that record and the approved metric glossary.
The draft states the North Star inputs it touches, if any: time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, verzuim, or manager satisfaction.
The analyst edits the Dutch, chooses the audience, and removes any count of who opened a report.
The analyst sends the note in Teams or Outlook and updates the SharePoint report list.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the Dutch text and the recipient list before the note is sent. Changes that affect processing the OR has consented to are held for the HR Director.
data_needed: Change record: object, old definition, new definition, effective date, dependent reports
Approved Dutch glossary of metric names
Audience list by report and site
Flag for whether the report was in the works-council consent file
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint metric register: change id, approver, time sent, audience, and a link to the message that was actually sent.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot can summarise a report and write DAX on a prepared semantic model. Non-English chat is not officially supported, which bears on Dutch notes to managers.

Works-council consent is required for systems that process personal data and for facilities that can observe presence, behaviour or performance. The test is the capability, and a missing consent can be nullified within one month.
A chatbot that interacts with people has to disclose that it is AI. A note sent by an unattended bot falls under that duty.

risks: A note that lists who opened a report records behaviour and can be a facility the works council must consent to under WOR article 27.
Dutch HR wording from a model can shift the meaning of verzuim, FTE or 90-day retention. Power BI Copilot does not officially support non-English chat.
If a bot posts into Teams on its own, article 50 requires it to say it is AI. The design avoids that by keeping the analyst as the sender.
Firing a note on every metadata edit will train managers to ignore the channel.
research_questions: How many certified-measure changes in a normal month are material to a manager, and how many would a broad trigger fire on?
How often does a Dutch draft need a full rewrite rather than a light edit?
Do managers act on the note, or do they still ask the HR business partner, so the work moves instead of shrinking?

tasks.short: Write specifications for workforce reports and dashboards.

today.trigger: An HR business partner, the HR Director or Finance asks for a new cut of the workforce figures, or an existing dashboard is rebuilt.
steps: Ask the requester which decision the report should support.
List measures, filters, sites, contract types, shift and the refresh time.
Write the specification in a SharePoint document, including who may see which rows.
Revise it when payroll, finance or HR disagree on the definition, then hand it to the build.
drudgery: Copying field lists from last year's specification
Renaming versions
Chasing comments spread across Teams and mail
today.time_sinks: Agreeing what headcount, FTE and verzuim mean across HR, payroll and finance takes longer than writing the field list.

lenses.faster: The blank page, the field list and the boilerplate on refresh and filters shrink. About two-thirds of the few hours a month remains, and that time goes to the definition and to row-level access.
lenses.autonomous: A logged request for a new or changed report starts a draft beside the analyst. Almost nothing runs alone, because the specification is the definition the company will calculate. The gate is the signed specification before anything is built.
lenses.ambitious: The works council receives a plain-language specification of each workforce report: purpose, fields, who sees it, and the fields that are excluded, including absence cause. That is a service the OR does not get as a standing product. Demand grows when a new report is proposed, and it stops there: the council's need follows the report calendar, not a cheaper unit price.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss formatting field lists and version tables. The analyst gets more of the argument about what 'still here and productive at day 90' means for a warehouse hire.
lenses.options: Two specifications of 90-day retention, one including flex workers and one limited to Noordhaven contracts, and two of verzuim, one with and one without the CAO waiting days, change the target the HR Director will manage. The drafts are the decision.
lenses.altitude: Specifications are edited from a draft instead of started empty. The analyst gains the right to certify a definition that HR, payroll and finance will share. The job becomes more expert, because the remaining work is the disputed meaning.
reach: The FP&A Analyst's write-up of the workforce assumptions in the headcount forecast. The analyst would need the finance close calendar and how AFAS maps wage costs to the general ledger.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst, with the requester, decides what the company will count and who may see it. A copilot can list fields and draft sentences. It cannot settle a dispute between payroll's paid FTE, finance's forecast FTE and HR's contract headcount, and it cannot decide that a proposed report would let the OR or a manager observe performance.
tasks.pattern_why: The specification is a judgment about definitions, access and purpose. The analyst has to lead that judgment, with a draft beside them. Publishing a specification without the analyst would turn a disputed definition into the company's standard. A single unattended model call is the wrong simplicity.

in_practice.trigger: A request for a new or changed workforce report is logged with the decision it is meant to support.
steps: The analyst records the decision, the grain, the sites, the contract types and whether flex workers are in scope.
A copilot drafts the field list, filters, refresh and row-level security from the certified dataset and the last approved specification.
The analyst rewrites the measure definitions in Dutch, including 90-day retention, time to hire, verzuim rate and duration, and FTE.
The draft states the purpose under the AVG and whether the report can show presence, behaviour or performance.
The requester signs, and the HR Director signs any definition that changes a North Star input. The works council receives the plain-language version before build.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst and the requester sign the specification before build. The HR Director signs definitions that change time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, verzuim or manager satisfaction. Reports that can observe performance or presence wait for works-council consent.
data_needed: The decision the report must support
Certified measures and their current definitions
Row-level security roles by site and HR role
Whether any field is health data or could show individual performance
The works-council consent status of the underlying processing
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history of the specification, with requester, analyst, HR Director sign-off, and the consent reference where one is required.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot writes DAX and summarises reports on Fabric F2+ or Premium. Without a prepared semantic model it can misinterpret the data, and non-English chat is not officially supported.
From 2 December 2027, AI used to evaluate worker performance or to allocate tasks from behaviour is high-risk: a competent overseer, logs kept for six months, and workers' representatives informed.
Absence data is health data under GDPR article 9. A specification that includes cause of sick leave asks for data the analytics model should not hold.

risks: A fluent specification can hide a live disagreement between HR, payroll and finance, and the build will then treat the draft as settled.
A specification for individual productivity, attrition or absence risk is a works-council matter now and can be a high-risk system from 2 December 2027.
DAX suggested on an unclear model can be copied into the specification and later certified by mistake.
Dutch prose from a copilot can name a measure correctly in English and wrongly in the words managers use.
research_questions: On which of headcount, FTE and verzuim do HR, payroll and finance already calculate different numbers?
What share of specification time is the field list, and what share is the argument about the decision and the definition?
Which reports proposed in the last year can observe presence, behaviour or performance and therefore need works-council consent before a specification is signed?

tasks.short: Turn the latest workforce trends into a recommended action.

today.trigger: The monthly HR meeting, preparation for the works council, or a site whose 90-day retention or verzuim looks different from last period.
steps: Pull the internal employment pack and the latest external clippings.
Compare sites, shifts and the previous period in Excel.
Write a short note or a few PowerPoint slides with one suggested action.
Walk the HR Director through the note and adjust the action.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same site comparison each month
Reformatting slides
Chasing one missing month or one late agency file
today.time_sinks: The first draft of the story takes longer than the decision in the meeting with the HR Director.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the comparison and writing the first draft disappears. About three and a half hours of the monthly six remain for checking the figures against the pack and for the recommendation itself.
lenses.autonomous: The signed monthly employment pack, or a move past a band the analyst has set with the HR Director, starts the run. One draft is written on its own from those certified figures and the approved external brief. The analyst gates the recommended action before it is treated as HR's position.
lenses.ambitious: The HR Director takes a site-level action on 90-day retention or verzuim every month, inside the month, instead of once a quarter. That decision happens far more often. Demand would grow if every site lead wanted a weekly action note, and weekly noise would make the actions worse, so the rhythm stays monthly unless a pre-agreed band is crossed.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the monthly slide from scratch. The analyst gets more of the conversation with the HR Director about what the company should actually do.
lenses.options: Three drafts, built from the same certified figures, change the action: add flex at the site, change week-one onboarding, or adjust pay within the CAO. Seeing all three, with what would have to be true for each, is what the HR Director decides on.
lenses.altitude: The month contains a decision meeting on a prepared brief. The analyst gains the right to put one recommended action, with sources, on the HR Director's agenda. The job becomes more expert on the call and loses the slide production.
reach: The HR Director's first draft of the monthly retention and verzuim narrative for the leadership meeting. The analyst would need the director's vocabulary toward the works council, and the line between a rate and a cause of absence.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst and the HR Director judge what is noise in a three-site warehouse operation, what the CAO and the flex agencies can actually absorb, and what the works council should hear. The model drafts from figures it is given. It does not invent the numbers, and it does not turn a site trend into a decision about an identifiable employee.
tasks.pattern_why: The path does not change from month to month: certified figures and the approved external brief go in, one sourced draft with several actions comes out, a person chooses. That is one model call inside a fixed workflow. An agent is unnecessary because the steps are known before the run starts.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly employment pack is signed, or 90-day retention or the verzuim rate at a site crosses a band agreed with the HR Director.
steps: The run reads only certified measures by site, shift and contract type, already suppressed below the agreed group size.
It attaches the latest approved labour-market brief and refuses to recompute any figure.
One model call drafts a Dutch note with two or three actions and the evidence for each, plus an explicit caveat where the source does not show a cause.
The analyst checks every number against the pack and drops any action aimed at a named person or an identifiable crew.
The HR Director accepts, edits or rejects the action, and the outcome is written on the brief.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the draft for factual match to the pack. The HR Director approves the action before it is HR's position. No recommendation is issued as a decision about an individual employee.
data_needed: Certified headcount, FTE, time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding completion, 90-day retention, verzuim rate and duration, by site and shift
The approved external brief and its source set
The agreed minimum group size
The band that triggers an out-of-cycle note
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint brief library: refresh id, sources, model name, analyst check, the action the HR Director accepted or rejected, and the date.

evidence.claim: Microsoft warns that faster access to workforce information does not, by itself, lead to better decisions.
Workday's customer trend data does not establish how much of the reported change AI caused. A recommendation note needs the same limit on what it claims.
GDPR article 22 bars a decision based solely on automated processing where the decision produces a significant effect on a person.
In a Visier survey, 48% of 1,000 US employees said they had exaggerated their use of AI. Self-reported time savings are a weak test of this note.

risks: A site-and-shift cell can identify one team lead or one night crew. The recommendation then functions as a judgment on a person.
The draft can state a cause for a rise in verzuim that the data cannot support, including a hint at diagnosis.
More frequent notes can create actions the operation cannot absorb, without improving 90-day retention.
Visier's survey is a reason to distrust a later claim that managers 'use the brief' unless the accepted actions are counted.
research_questions: Over the last four leadership meetings, which workforce figures actually changed a staffing, onboarding or pay action?
What group size will HR and the works council accept so a site-and-shift figure does not point to one crew?
After one brief with a wrong figure, do the HR Director and the site leads keep using the next one?

tasks.short: Test that the workforce figures match the agreed needs.

today.trigger: A pack is about to go to management or the works council, or a manager says a number is wrong.
steps: Export headcount from Power BI and from AFAS by site and contract type and compare them.
Spot-check verzuim percentages, time to hire and 90-day retention against source lists.
Look for small groups that a reader could identify, and for absence-cause text that should never have been extracted.
Ask HR administration to correct AFAS, then test again after the next refresh.
drudgery: Ticking row counts by hand
Exporting the same lists to Excel every month
Re-testing known gaps in end dates and open absence records
today.time_sinks: The manual tie-out before each pack, and the wait while someone corrects the source, consumes most of the half day a month.

lenses.faster: Hand tie-outs, repeated exports and re-checking known gaps disappear. About two hours a month remain, from about six, for failures, for a new definition, and for asking HR administration or an agency to correct the source.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract and Power BI refresh start the checks. The rules run on their own and mark a refresh publishable only when the required rules pass. The analyst gates every failure, and HR administration corrects AFAS.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers, between 150 and 300 people depending on the season, enter the same tie-out as employees: agency hours against the order, by site. Today their figures sit in three portals and are checked only when an invoice looks wrong. Demand grows in peak season, when the swing is large and Finance disputes hours.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking row counts. The analyst gets the failures that mean a real break, such as a site leaving absence records open or an agency file that does not match the order.
lenses.options: A strict tie-out and a tie-out that allows the known lag between the nightly extract and payroll close produce different lists of 'broken' figures. The choice changes who is called, HR administration or payroll, and whether this month's pack waits. Both results are shown before the analyst picks.
lenses.altitude: The morning after refresh starts from the exception list. The analyst gains the right to stop a required figure from publishing when a check fails. The job becomes more expert on whether a figure can be trusted.
reach: The Payroll Specialist's people-count tie-out at month close, and the Bookkeeper's check that a flex invoice matches ordered hours. The analyst would need the payroll close calendar and the hour fields in the three agency portals. Gross-to-net stays with payroll.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst decides whether a failed rule is a source error, a definition that has changed, or a normal timing lag around month close, and who is allowed to correct AFAS, Recruitee or an agency file. The rules can flag the case. They cannot make that call, and they must not write absence-cause text into the log.
tasks.pattern_why: Tie-out tolerances, missing end dates, a populated absence-cause column, minimum group size and flex hours against orders are rules that can be written down. They should run on the refresh with no model in the path, because a model that 'explains' a payroll figure can invent the explanation. The person sees the failures.

in_practice.trigger: Each nightly refresh of the AFAS extract into the Power BI dataset, and any manual reload of an agency hour file.
steps: The refresh runs the written rules: headcount and FTE by site and contract type, hire dates against Recruitee, verzuim from start and end dates only, group size, and flex hours against orders.
A required figure is marked publishable for that refresh only when its rules pass.
Failures are written as rule id plus record keys. The log records that a forbidden field was present and does not store the field contents.
The analyst assigns each failure to HR administration, payroll, a recruiter or the agency-file owner.
Failed rules are run again after the correction and before the analyst signs a required pack.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst handles every failed rule and decides whether the pack waits. HR administration corrects employee and absence records in AFAS. The analyst does not publish a required figure while its rule is failing.
data_needed: AFAS employee, contract, site, start date and end date
Absence start and end, with cause and diagnosis columns tested for presence and excluded from the analytics tables
Recruitee application and hire dates for time to hire and 90-day retention
Studytube certificate expiry for forklift, VCA and food safety
Agency order hours and reported hours by site
Agreed tolerances and the agreed minimum group size
in_practice.logs_to: A table in the analytics workspace, one row per rule per refresh: rule id, pass or fail, keys, assignee, and correction time. Kept with the monthly pack.

evidence.claim: Missing contract end dates and absence records left open are expressible as rules. The digest rates that kind of AFAS check as model knowledge, with HR administration correcting the source.

The Dutch Data Protection Authority fined a company EUR 15,000 partly for recording the cause of sick leave. A test should fail when cause text reaches the analytics tables, and the log must not copy that text.

A consultant's reading of works-council law holds that totals drawn from a tool which stores per-person rows can still require consent. Group-size suppression belongs in the test, not only in the visual.

risks: A check that reads absence-cause text can copy health data into the exception log. The log has to record presence of the column, not its contents.
Rules can miss the defects managers actually complain about and flag ordinary month-end lags, after which people ignore the list.
Three agency portals define hours differently. A false mismatch on flex hours will land on the bookkeepers every peak season.
Stopping publication on a failed rule can delay payroll close if the tolerance is set tighter than the nightly extract deserves.
research_questions: What share of figure errors reported in the last six months would these rules have caught?
Who corrects AFAS, Recruitee and the agency files, and can they do it before payroll close?
Does matching named flex workers to agency hours need a new purpose and works-council consent?

tasks.short: Compare Noordhaven pay and hiring with the outside labour market.

today.trigger: The annual reward review, a warehouse or driver role that stays open, or a staffing agency that proposes a higher rate.
steps: Collect published wage and vacancy signals for warehouse and transport roles around the three sites.
Read the CAO scales, Noordhaven's bands and the current flex share.
Compare the three agencies' rates with the last order.
Write a note for the Compensation and Benefits Specialist and the HR Director.
drudgery: Reading job ads one by one
Reconciling survey tables that use different job titles
Chasing an outdated rate card
today.time_sinks: Making an outside wage comparable with shift allowances, irregular hours and the CAO takes most of the few hours in the month this is done.

lenses.faster: The first pass through public vacancy counts and stored rate cards disappears. About three hours of the monthly five remain for judging comparability and for the conversation with Compensation and Benefits.
lenses.autonomous: A new agency rate card, the reward calendar, or a role family whose time to hire crosses an agreed band starts the run. The comparison draft is written on its own from files already stored. The analyst and the Compensation and Benefits Specialist gate it before it enters a pay proposal.
lenses.ambitious: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist receives a site-level comparison of CAO bands, agency rates and public vacancy pressure before the reward round, as a service that today is a one-off spreadsheet. If it were cheap, recruiters would ask for it each time a driver, warehouse or team-lead role opens, and that demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss maintaining a scrapbook of job ads. The analyst gets more of the pay-band conversation with Compensation and Benefits, where warehouse allowances and night work decide whether a signal is real.
lenses.options: Three comparisons change the proposal: base pay only, base pay plus shift and irregular-hours allowances, and full cost including the agency margin. One of those can say Noordhaven sits above the market while another says the night shift sits below it. The Compensation and Benefits Specialist has to see all three before choosing.
lenses.altitude: The comparison is waiting before the reward conversation. The analyst gains the right to mark an outside wage signal as usable or unusable for a Noordhaven role. The job becomes more expert on comparability.
reach: The Recruiter's scan of the local market when a warehouse or driver role stays open. The analyst would need Recruitee's stage definitions and which roles the CAO covers. Contact with candidates and agencies stays with the recruiter.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst and the Compensation and Benefits Specialist know whether an outside rate includes night allowance, weekend work or only a base hourly wage, and what room the CAO leaves. A model can line up stored figures. It cannot decide that a signal is comparable, and it must not propose an individual wage.
tasks.pattern_why: The inputs are messy text and rate cards, and the output is one checkable comparison with a fixed structure. One model call can draft it from files already collected under the source-brief task. Calls to agencies and the pay decision stay with people, which is a gate on a fixed workflow, not a reason to leave the draft manual or to use an agent.

in_practice.trigger: The reward-cycle date set by Compensation and Benefits, a new rate card from one of the three agencies, or a Recruitee role family that breaches the agreed time-to-hire band.
steps: The run takes the approved labour-market brief, Noordhaven's bands, the CAO scales and the latest agency rates. It does not search the open web.
One model call drafts three comparisons: base pay, pay plus allowances, and cost including agency margin, by site and role family.
Every outside figure keeps the citation already checked on the source brief.
The analyst marks each signal usable or unusable and writes the reason in Dutch.
Compensation and Benefits accepts a version before it is used in a pay or flex proposal.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst marks comparability. The Compensation and Benefits Specialist approves any version that will be used in a pay proposal or an agency negotiation. The recruiter keeps contact with candidates and agencies.
data_needed: Approved labour-market brief and its stored sources
Noordhaven pay bands by role family and site
CAO scales and the allowances that apply on shift
Current agency rates and flex share by site
Time-to-hire by role family from Recruitee
No individual candidate records from outside employers
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint reward folder: version, sources, usability marks, model name, and the Compensation and Benefits decision.

evidence.claim: No source opened for this digest reports a Dutch logistics employer automating a CAO-to-market pay comparison, or a works-council decision on that comparison.
Published workforce trend reports can be read as proof of a cause they do not establish. A pay comparison has the same limit.
Faster access to workforce information does not, by itself, lead to better decisions.

risks: Treating base pay as if it included night or weekend allowance can push a CAO position the wrong way.
Job ads are a weak guide to what a competitor pays and can contain personal data Noordhaven has no purpose to store.
Compensation and Benefits may still commission a paid survey and set this brief aside, so the drafting time is pure addition.
There is no documented Dutch result in the digest, so the expected time cut may not appear.
research_questions: Is there a public or purchased source whose job definitions match Noordhaven's shifts and allowances closely enough to move a CAO position?
Would Compensation and Benefits still buy a full survey and ignore an internal brief?
Do the vacancy files being stored contain personal data, and is there a recorded purpose for keeping them?

tasks.short: Prepare the required reports on employment, absence and hiring.

today.trigger: Month close, a works-council meeting, or a standing request from the HR Director, payroll or finance.
steps: Take the AFAS employment, contract and absence figures from the nightly extract or a fresh export.
Build headcount, FTE, verzuim rate, time to hire and 90-day retention in Power BI or Excel.
Add flex hours from the agency files and certificate totals from Studytube.
Write a short commentary, circulate the pack, and correct it when questions come back.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same pivots each month
Waiting for late agency files
Rewriting the commentary from scratch
Sending versions that then get forwarded as attachments
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the pack and checking it against AFAS, before anyone will use it, takes most of the half day.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding pivots and pasting commentary from scratch disappears, because the nightly refresh and a fixed pack already exist as the base. Sign-off, breaks and questions remain about half of today's half day, a little over two hours a month.
lenses.autonomous: The payroll calendar starts the pack: working day 2 for management and finance, and the OR meeting date for the council. The refresh fills a fixed report on its own. The analyst gates sign-off of each required pack before it is sent.
lenses.ambitious: The Controller receives, on the finance close calendar, a workforce pack that uses the same FTE definition as HR. Finance does not get that as a certified feed today. If the feed is cheap to slice, FP&A will ask for cost-centre and flex-up/flex-down versions, and that demand will grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the headcount pivot. The analyst gets more time on whether the 90-day retention figure is true and on what the OR and the HR Director should take from it.
lenses.options: Packs that place flex inside the verzuim and retention rates, and packs that keep flex beside them, change whether a site looks like an absence problem or a mix problem. Showing both versions, with group-size suppression applied, changes the action the Controller and the HR Director will take.
lenses.altitude: On working day 2 the pack is waiting for sign-off instead of being built. The analyst gains the right to certify the employment figures the OR, the HR Director and finance use. Expertise moves toward the certification and the breaks.
reach: The Controller's workforce schedule inside the monthly finance pack. The analyst would need the controller's calendar and the difference between contract headcount and paid FTE.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst certifies that the pack matches AFAS, that verzuim is a rate and a duration, and that a total cannot be unwound to a small night crew. The refresh can fill the pages. It cannot sign a figure the works council or an auditor will rely on, and it cannot decide that this month's break is acceptable.
tasks.pattern_why: Required employment figures must tie to AFAS through a refresh, a locked dataset and a fixed report. A model narrative is a poor place to produce those numbers, because a wrong sentence about verzuim or retention spreads as fast as the pack. The simplest path that works is the refresh plus a template, with a person signing every required issue.

in_practice.trigger: Working day 2 after month end for the management and finance pack, and the published OR meeting date for the council pack.
steps: The nightly AFAS extract refreshes the certified dataset. Rules from the test task must be passing for every figure in the pack.
A fixed Power BI report fills headcount, FTE, verzuim rate and duration, time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, flex hours and certificate-compliance percentages.
Cells below the agreed group size are suppressed in the OR pack and in the management pack.
The analyst reviews breaks, writes the short commentary in the template, and signs the pack.
The signed pack is distributed by subscription to the HR Director, HR business partners, payroll, the Controller and, on its own calendar, the works council.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst signs each required pack. The HR Director signs the version that goes to the works council. A figure with a failing tie-out stays out of the pack.
data_needed: Certified measures already passing the nightly rules
Payroll period calendar and OR meeting dates
Flex hour totals by site and agency
Studytube compliance percentages for forklift, VCA and food safety
Finance's FTE definition, so the controller's pack names it
The agreed minimum group size
in_practice.logs_to: The Power BI subscription record plus a sign-off line stored with the pack: refresh id, analyst, time, recipients, and any figure withheld.

evidence.claim: Power BI already refreshes on a nightly AFAS extract in this company. Copilot on that model can summarise a prepared report and write DAX, and it can misinterpret data when the model is not prepared. The required numbers themselves come from the refresh, not from the copilot.

Absence data is health data. Reporting verzuim as rates and durations, with cause fields kept out of the extract, is the boundary set by GDPR article 9 and by the Dutch fine for recording sick-leave causes.
Works-council consent covers personal-data systems and facilities that can observe presence, behaviour or performance. Capability is the test.

risks: A site-level verzuim or retention total can be unwound to a small crew, especially on nights. The OR can treat that as personal data even when the page shows a total.
A wrong certified definition, refreshed every night, reaches managers faster than the old Excel pack did.
Sign-off becomes a rubber stamp if the pack is long and the analyst no longer rebuilds it.
Including absence cause, even in a commentary sentence, repeats the kind of processing that drew a EUR 15,000 AP fine.
research_questions: Which current packs are required by the works council, an auditor or a filing, and which are habit and can stop?
Can the AFAS extract be built so diagnosis and cause of absence never land in the analytics workspace?
Does the works council regard a site-level verzuim and retention report as needing consent when the page shows only totals?

tasks.short: Keep the shared templates and metric definitions up to date.

today.trigger: Someone cannot find the current template, or a definition has changed and older files are still in use.
steps: Search SharePoint for the latest specification, DAX note, pack template or metric sheet.
Copy it, rename it and edit the part that changed.
Answer mail about which file is the right one.
Archive the old copy when someone remembers.
drudgery: Duplicate files with unclear names
Templates that still use last year's FTE definition
Copies forwarded in Outlook that never return to the library
today.time_sinks: Finding the current file, and repairing copies that have drifted, takes longer than the edit itself.

lenses.faster: Hunting for the current file and retyping unchanged sections shrinks. About two-thirds of the monthly four hours remains for deciding which document is the standard and for repairing a definition that drifted.
lenses.autonomous: A review date, or a change in the metric register, raises a reminder and a draft revision. Certification does not run alone. The analyst gates which file is the standard others may use.
lenses.ambitious: The two Learning and Development Specialists get one certified view of forklift, VCA and food-safety certificate status that covers warehouse shifts and the flex workers who must hold those certificates on site. They build that list by hand today. Demand grows in peak season as flex headcount rises, and it depends on a clear purpose for using agency workers' certificate data.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss renaming files and chasing old versions. The analyst gets more of the work of keeping one agreed meaning of FTE, verzuim and time to hire.
lenses.options: Putting HR's FTE, payroll's paid FTE and finance's forecast FTE in one register, each with its purpose, changes whether the Controller and the Payroll Specialist will adopt the library. A single unlabeled definition looks tidy and will be rejected. The three labeled drafts are what make the adoption decision possible.
lenses.altitude: Review dates drive the week. The analyst gains the right to retire a template and name its replacement as the one HR and Finance may use. The job becomes more expert as the keeper of one language.
reach: The Learning and Development Specialist's certificate status lists for forklift, VCA and food safety. The analyst would need to know which certificates are a legal condition for the work and which are company policy, and the purpose for holding that data.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst decides which document is the standard and when an old definition must be retired even though a team still likes it. A copilot can draft an update and point at stale copies. It cannot decide that payroll's paid-hour definition and HR's headcount definition are both legitimate and must stay labeled, or that a template is fit for the works council to read.
tasks.pattern_why: Maintaining the library is curation. The analyst decides what is standard, with a draft and a list of stale copies beside them. Review dates can be a simple reminder, but choosing and rewriting the canonical definition is the person's work. An unattended job would certify a template nobody has accepted.

in_practice.trigger: A certified template reaches its review date, or a definition in the metric register changes.
steps: The register lists each template: owner, purpose, metric ids, review date, and whether works-council consent covers the processing it describes.
A copilot drafts the changed sections from the register and flags other files in the library that still use the old wording.
The analyst rewrites the Dutch definition and labels HR, payroll and finance versions where the meanings differ.
The nightly tests are pointed at the certified measures named in the template before the analyst marks it current.
The analyst retires the previous file and tells HR administration, payroll, L&D and FP&A which file is current.
in_practice.human_gate: Only the analyst marks a template certified. A draft can sit in the library as a draft. HR administration, payroll and L&D use the certified copy.
data_needed: Template id, owner, purpose, review date and status
Metric ids and the current certified wording
Audience and the works-council consent reference where the template describes personal-data processing
Studytube certificate types for forklift, VCA and food safety
Which FTE definition payroll and finance each require
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint register of templates: version, owner, certifier, review date, and the metric-register change that triggered the revision.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot can draft DAX on a prepared semantic model and can misinterpret a model that is not prepared. A DAX snippet in the library is only as safe as the measure it was drafted from.
Works-council consent turns on capability to observe presence, behaviour or performance. A template that describes such a report is part of what the council needs to see.
Keeping one definition of FTE across HR, payroll and finance is a local governance task. The digest gives no product case that substitutes for the analyst's choice of the standard.

risks: HR, payroll and finance can each keep a private meaning of FTE. A library that hides the difference will be ignored, and a library that collapses it will be wrong for payroll.
A rewritten DAX template can change a certified number if it is filed without the nightly tests pointed at it.
Old files in mailboxes will outlive a clean library, so site managers may keep using last year's definition.
A certificate template that names flex workers pulls agency training data into Noordhaven's processing and needs a purpose before it is certified.
research_questions: How many live copies of the FTE and verzuim definitions exist on SharePoint and in mail, and who uses each?
Does payroll's definition of paid hours require a second template that must stay labeled rather than merged?
Will HR administration and L&D use a copilot rewrite of a template on a starter or a certificate file without a side-by-side check?

role.altitude: The week moves from assembling packs to certifying the workforce figures Noordhaven uses. The analyst sets the definitions of headcount, FTE, time to hire, 90-day retention and verzuim, who may see a cut, and whether a refresh is fit to publish. HR business partners and site managers work from that pack. The analyst spends the remaining time on failed checks, the works council's questions and the labour-market call. The job becomes more expert.
reach: Compensation and Benefits: the first collection of market wage figures, once the analyst can file CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer scales and the warehouse CAO allowances against Noordhaven's bands.
HR Business Partners: passing material dashboard changes to site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, once the analyst has each site's audience and the OR information routine.
FP&A Analysts: writing down the workforce assumptions in the headcount forecast, once the analyst knows the finance calendar and the AFAS general-ledger mapping of wage costs.
Controller: the workforce schedule in the monthly finance pack, using one named FTE definition.
Payroll Specialist and the accounts-payable Bookkeepers: the people-count tie-out and the match of flex invoices to ordered hours. Gross-to-net and the vendor payment stay where they are.
Recruiters: a sourced scan when a warehouse or driver role stays open. Candidate and agency contact stays with the recruiters.
Learning and Development Specialists: one certificate-status view for forklift, VCA and food safety, once purpose and legal-versus-policy status are clear.
The HR Director's first draft of the monthly retention and verzuim narrative. The director keeps the decision and the relationship with the works council.
role.ceiling_note: One FTE at EUR 78 an hour cannot review every site question and every agency-file exception in a peak week, when flex headcount is near 300 and the warehouses run nights. Absence is health data, so casework under the Wet verbetering poortwachter stays outside this role, as does payroll gross-to-net. Works-council consent, GDPR article 22 and the high-risk rules for performance evaluation from 2 December 2027 limit scoring of individuals. Dutch text still needs a person: Power BI Copilot does not officially support non-English chat. The digest shows no Dutch result and no works-council decision to copy.
skills_to_grow: CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the warehouse CAO: scales, shift and irregular-hours allowances, and the boundary between an employee and a flex worker.
AVG and WOR in practice: purpose limitation, article 9 health data, consent files, and group size the works council will accept.
AFAS Profit's contract, absence and payroll-component structure, and the link from wage costs to the general ledger.
Power BI semantic models: row-level security, certified measures, refresh failure and a test the OR can read.
Recruitee stages and Studytube certificate records, well enough to join them to AFAS without inventing a 90-day or compliance figure.
Writing a metric definition that a site manager, a payroll specialist and the works council will read the same way.
role.ambitious_version: Noordhaven runs one workforce measurement standard for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, for day and night, and for employees and flex workers. On the second working day the HR Director sees 90-day retention and the verzuim rate and duration, tied to AFAS, with a sourced note on what moved. The Controller sees the same FTE on the finance calendar. Compensation and Benefits sees a labour-market comparison before a pay decision. The works council can read what is measured and what is excluded. The analyst's week is the standard, the failed checks and the exceptions. Individual scores for attrition or absence stay outside that ambition.
